info.title: kestrel operator
info.summary: The boundary a Client reaches a control plane over.
info.description: Server-sent events down, JSON up, plain HTTP. It authenticates nobody, so the control plane serves it on a listener of its own, apart from the link, and binds that listener to loopback unless told otherwise. A remote control plane is reached through a tunnel. Every operation refuses with 403, and does nothing, a request whose Host is not loopback, or whose Origin, when it sends one, is not exactly http:// followed by that Host.

A key two harnesses offer appears once for each, sharing its revision and authentication evidence but never its model-use evidence. An empty slot is absent; the harness catalogue describes what could be saved. Nothing read here is the material, a hash of it, a login file or a provider's own words.

put.summary: Save material for a catalogued Sign-in Method.
put.description: A subscription is held in the Operator's own Profile, declared after the Operator when they have none; a key is held as the Organization's Provider Credential the method fills. Nobody is asked which. The value is checked for shape before anything is stored, and a key whose provider documents an authenticated model-metadata read is checked that way, bounded to ten seconds; nothing ever spends model usage. A provider refusing the key itself is 422 and keeps what was saved before; a refusal about permission, credit or another matter saves the key unchecked. A provider that cannot be asked, times out or limits the rate saves it unchecked and answers 503 carrying what was saved. Material replaced while this was being checked is 409, and the replacement stands.

put.summary: Replace a GitHub Integration's App private key.
put.description: The replacement is checked against GitHub first: it must sign as the same App, mint for the same installation and reach the same repository. Only then does it replace the stored key, in one write that bumps the revision, so an installation token minted with the previous key is never handed out afterwards. A replacement that is not accepted, an App that no longer reaches its installation or repository, a rate limit or an outage saves nothing and leaves the previous key in use. Maintenance that lands while GitHub is being asked refuses the replacement with 409. The key is never returned.

get.summary: Read the Organization's queue: the limits, their occupancy, the queued Sessions in dispatch order, the Waiting Sessions and the unbriefed ones.
get.description: Queued Sessions appear in the order they were enqueued. Each one ready for dispatch apart from the shared Active-Work Slot pool is numbered from 1; one that is not carries no number and names every reason that holds it, derived by the rules dispatch applies. A queued Session whose Workspace has no Brief waits only on its Instance. Waiting Sessions follow, unnumbered, with any held input and why their next turn has not started. Unbriefed Sessions follow those, beside them: they hold their Instances and no Active-Work Slot, are never numbered, and carry the step they are preparing on and any message held for their Brief. Nothing is estimated. The Active-Work Slot limit and the Compute driver are the ones the dispatching work role recorded, or no work role is dispatching; the pool belongs to the control plane and every Organization shares it, so other Organizations' occupants are counted and never named. Reading changes nothing.

get.summary: Stream a Workspace's Transcript.
get.description: Replays every entry after `Last-Event-ID`, in order, each as an `entry` event whose id is the cursor that resumes after it. A read that follows then stays open and delivers entries as they are appended; the stream ends with an `end` event once the Workspace is sealed, or at once for a read that does not follow. A cursor that names no position in this Transcript is refused rather than silently restarting the walk. A follow that stays open past caught-up registers a follower: it is sent one `follower` event carrying its id and lease, then a `presence` event carrying the whole current set, and a new `presence` event whenever the set changes. Presence events carry no id and never move the cursor, and a read that does not follow registers nobody.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: The Workspace whose Transcript is read, by its generated name, its identifier, any unambiguous prefix of its identifier, or `latest`.

parameters.name: follow
parameters.description: Whether to stay open for entries appended after the ones already recorded.

parameters.name: as
parameters.description: The person this follow joins the Workspace's presence as, by the participant name rule; naming an Agent in the Organization is refused. Only a read that stays open past caught-up registers a follower.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The id of the last entry this reader was delivered. Absent means from the beginning.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Comma-separated Transcript kinds. The cursor advances across every examined seq, including omitted kinds.

parameters.name: summaries
parameters.description: Summarize omitted narration and detail, across every shared-state boundary even when shared state is not selected. With every kind selected there are no summaries.

parameters.name: first_seq
parameters.description: Inclusive first seq of an Activity expansion. Select every kind to read its entries.

parameters.name: last_seq
parameters.description: Inclusive last seq of an Activity expansion; must be at least first_seq. The finite range ends when caught up.

200.description: The stream is open. Each event carries an entry, the end of the stream, a follower registration or the whole presence set as its data, and its name as its event name.

post.summary: Extend a Workspace follow's presence lease.
post.description: Extends the follower's lease to a full period from now. An unknown follower, or one whose lease has already passed, is refused: a lapsed follow reconnects and registers again rather than being revived.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The follower id a `follower` event carried.

get.summary: Fetch a referenced Transcript payload within its owning Workspace

410.description: The entry expired and its payload content was removed

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: The Workspace whose Transcript is read, by its generated name, its identifier, any unambiguous prefix of its identifier, or `latest`.

schema.description: Owning workspace UUID, entry seq and field, separated by colons.

get.summary: Stream the Organization's change notices.
get.description: Opens with an `open` event, then sends a `change` event naming each Workspace, Session or queue that changed, at most once per resource per 250 ms. A notice says what changed, never what it changed to. No event carries an id and `Last-Event-ID` is ignored: a notice is a hint to refetch, never a cursor. A subscriber that falls behind the bounded buffer is sent `resync` instead of a silent gap.

200.description: The stream is open. `open` and `resync` mean every subscribed view must be refetched; `change` names one resource.

put.summary: Reserve a browser tab's one event stream.
put.description: Answers a token that opens the stream and addresses its subscriptions. A reservation with no open connection for the follower lease period, 60 seconds unless configured otherwise, is forgotten, and a reservation is forgotten as soon as its connection closes: after any drop the tab reserves again and re-subscribes each subscription from the last cursor it saw. Reservations and subscriptions live only in the serve role's memory, and a control plane holds at most 256 reservations.

get.summary: Open a reserved stream.
get.description: Carries the events of every subscription made under the token, before or after it opens, interleaved. Every event names its subscription, and an entry, Activity or cursor event carries its own Transcript's cursor; no event carries an SSE id and `Last-Event-ID` resumes nothing. A subscription whose own stream would end with `end` sends it and is forgotten. One cut off for any other reason, such as a follower lease that passed, closes the whole stream, so the tab resumes every subscription the same way.

put.summary: Subscribe a reserved stream to an Organization's notices or a Workspace's Transcript.
put.description: Starts the subscription under the id the tab chose, replacing and ending any it already held under that id. A `notices` subscription opens with `open`, as the Organization's change stream does; a `transcript` subscription follows the Workspace's Transcript from `after` exactly as a per-resource follow from that `Last-Event-ID` does, registering a follower, anonymous unless it names a `participant`, once caught up whose lease the tab renews through the Workspace's follower lease. A reservation holds at most 32 subscriptions.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The tab's name for the subscription, every event of which carries it.

delete.summary: End one of a reserved stream's subscriptions.
delete.description: Ends the subscription and removes its follower at once. An id the reservation does not hold is already ended.

Refused.description: The control plane refused the request, with a typed Diagnostic (ADR-0052) where its producer is typed and a plain Refusal where it is not yet; only `kind` tells them apart. 400 is a malformed request; 403 is a forbidden action, such as changing a Held Message its author did not write; 404 is a missing or ambiguous reference; 409 is a state conflict, or a declined operation not yet typed; 410 is an expired resource; 422 is an invalid field value; 503 is a control plane that could not answer; 504 is an Instance that did not answer a read within 10 s. 400, 503 and 504 are always typed.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before asking again. Present on a 503 only when the database was busy, which asking again can clear; the Diagnostic's `retry_after_seconds` carries the same value.

command.description: The default ACP command; explicit harness-command configuration remains authoritative.

availability.description: Whether the configured image declares this harness, read from the image at this request. Null only in the catalogue's own data, never in a response.

HarnessAvailability.description: `available` and `not_carried` come from inspecting the configured image's `dev.kestrel.harnesses` label (ADR-0048). `unavailable` means the inspection failed, so nothing is claimed about the harness, and carries why. `unchecked` means the compute driver runs no image.

identity.description: The immutable local image ID the reference resolved to when it was inspected.

SignInMaterial.description: Never answered back, logged or kept in a diagnostic.

value.description: The token or key, or the login file's whole contents, as the method's input says.

SavedSignIn.description: Material saved for a catalogued Sign-in Method, as everything but the Session it is handed to sees it.

revision.description: Minted for every accepted write of the material, a generic Profile or Provider Credential write included, and never reused.

model_use.description: The latest result per model of this harness using this revision. A result for one model never stands for another.

reference.description: The Profile's name, or the Provider Credential's variable.

AuthenticationEvidence.description: Whether this revision authenticates, which says nothing of whether a harness can use a model with it. `login_completed` is a finished vendor sign-in and `credential_accepted` a provider accepting the one request recorded in `provider_check`; neither is a model call. Expiry and lack of coverage are only ever established by evidence.

ProviderCheck.description: One authenticated model-metadata read. Only `rejected` says the provider refused the credential; `inconclusive` is a refusal about permission, credit or another matter; `unavailable` includes a timeout and a rate or quota limit.

provider_error.description: The provider's error type or code, never its message.

PayloadReference.description: A body field exceeding 65536 bytes, fetched under its owning Workspace; message, thought and brief text use raw UTF-8, while plans, batched messages and tool input/results use compact JSON.

earlier_reports.description: The last report of each other Instance the Workspace has had, newest first, each history for its own Instance.
The last report of each other Instance the Workspace has had, newest first, each history for its own Instance.
The last report of each other Instance the Workspace has had, newest first, each history for its own Instance.

WorkLastReport.description: The last complete work report any of the Workspace's Instances sent, kept across link loss, release and restart. It is history: it is no evidence of current Unpublished Work, authorizes no seal or release, and makes no Files or Changes read live.

WorkNoReport.description: No Instance of the Workspace has sent a work report.

instance.description: The Instance that sent the report.

current_instance.description: Whether the Workspace still holds that Instance. When false the report belongs to an Instance it released or replaced, never to its current one.

path.description: The directory listed, or empty for the Workspace's repositories.

total.description: How many entries the directory holds, including any not listed.

git.description: Absent for a repository in the Workspace's list of them.

max_live_instances.description: The most active, idle, or held Instances this Organization may keep live. Null means unbounded.

RepositoryPurpose.description: `declaration`, the default, takes every transport a Project does. `public_setup` takes only an HTTPS address or GitHub shorthand, since public-repository setup selects no Integration.

address.description: What a declaration holds and a checkout clones.

checkout_directory.description: The directory under the Workspace the repository is checked out into.

repositories.description: The repositories the work happens against, in order: an http(s)://, ssh://, git:// or file:// URL, an scp-style `user@host:path`, a local path on the Instance beginning `/`, `./` or `../`, or `owner/repo` or `github.com/owner/repo`, which is held as its HTTPS `.git` address.

model.description: The model it works with. Absent or null names none, and the Harness's own default is the answer.

mode.description: The mode it works in. Absent or null names none, and the Harness's own default is the answer.

thought_level.description: The thought level it works at. Absent or null names none, and the Harness's own default is the answer.

brief.description: The Brief the Workspace starts with, handed to the agent exactly as given.

credentials.description: Provider Credentials the Organization holds from this start on, each replacing any it holds under the same variable.

created.description: Whether the start declared it, rather than finding it declared.

Opened.description: A Workspace and the first Session its open enqueued, in one transaction.

filter.description: A CloudEvents filter of exact, prefix, suffix, all, any, or not.

every.description: A duration such as `1h`, counted from the declaration, in place of a filter.

cron.description: Five fields of minute, hour, day of the month, month and day of the week, such as `0 9 * * 1-5`, in place of a filter or an interval.

zone.description: The IANA time zone a cron expression is read in, such as `America/New_York`.

on_open_workspace.description: What a firing that correlates to an open Workspace does: continues its waiting Session, or starts a new Session with this Trigger's Agent. Absent continues.

model.description: The model its Sessions run with. Omitted, the Agent's, then the Harness's default.

mode.description: The mode its Sessions run in. Omitted, the Agent's, then the Harness's default.

thought_level.description: The thought level its Sessions run at. Omitted, the Agent's, then the Harness's default.

admits_outsiders.description: Whether the filter fires for Events from people outside the Organization.

model.description: The model its Sessions run with, or null for the Agent's or Harness's default.

mode.description: The mode its Sessions run in, or null for the Agent's or Harness's default.

thought_level.description: The thought level its Sessions run at, or null for the Agent's or Harness's default.

applied.description: Whether a trigger file declared it, rather than flags.

integration.description: The GitHub Integration the issue is read through; named with `issue`.

issue.description: Render against the Event a dispatch of this issue would record, recording nothing. Excludes `event`.

declared.description: A trigger file, to test the Trigger as it declares it rather than as it was applied.

would.description: What a firing would do now: open a Workspace, continue the waiting Session of the open one it correlates to, start a new Session there, or ignore a correlation miss.

triggers.description: Each Trigger the file applies, keyed by its name; `{}` removes every Trigger a file applied.

model.description: The model its Sessions run with. Omitted, the Agent's, then the Harness's default.

mode.description: The mode its Sessions run in. Omitted, the Agent's, then the Harness's default.

thought_level.description: The thought level its Sessions run at. Omitted, the Agent's, then the Harness's default.

work_role.description: The last recorded dispatch configuration, or null when none is known. This record does not establish work-role liveness.

driver.description: The Compute driver it provisions Instances with: the Environment work is provisioned in, read-only.

limit.description: The recorded Active-Work Slot limit, or null when dispatch configuration is unknown.

occupied.description: Every working or trailing Session on the control plane: the pool it counts against is shared by every Organization.

occupants.description: This Organization's working and trailing Sessions, in the order they were enqueued.

elsewhere.description: Occupants of other Organizations, counted and never named.

Occupant.description: A Session holding an Active-Work Slot. A trailing one answered its Turn while work its agent started still runs; it is never among the Waiting Sessions.

limit.description: The Organization's live Instance limit, or null when unbounded.

count.description: The Instances counted against it, idle ones retained for Unpublished Work included.

counted.description: The counted Instances that can be named.

position.description: Global order among eligible requests for an Active-Work Slot, including queued Sessions, Held Messages and first Briefs. Retained while slots are full; null when blocked, not requesting a slot, or dispatch configuration is unknown.

reasons.description: Current blockers and predecessors for this request, computed by the scheduler. Other Organizations are counted without naming their Sessions.

WaitingSession.description: A Session between Turns. Held Messages request an Active-Work Slot and have a global position when eligible.

pending_since.description: When the oldest input held for its next turn arrived, or null while it is only waiting for a turn.

reasons.description: Current blockers and predecessors for this request, computed by the scheduler. Other Organizations are counted without naming their Sessions.

position.description: Global order among eligible requests for an Active-Work Slot, including queued Sessions, Held Messages and first Briefs. Retained while slots are full; null when blocked, not requesting a slot, or dispatch configuration is unknown.

UnbriefedSession.description: A Session preparing or ready for its first Turn. Provisioning is unnumbered; a written Brief competes for an Active-Work Slot once the harness is ready.

preparing.description: The step it is preparing on: provisioning from claim until its supervisor connects, cloning until its checkout is reported, starting_harness until the harness is up, and harness_ready once it is.

pending_since.description: When the oldest message held for its Brief arrived, or null while it holds none.

position.description: Global order among eligible requests for an Active-Work Slot, including queued Sessions, Held Messages and first Briefs. Retained while slots are full; null when blocked, not requesting a slot, or dispatch configuration is unknown.

reasons.description: Current blockers and predecessors for this request, computed by the scheduler. Other Organizations are counted without naming their Sessions.

brief_since.description: When its unstarted Brief was written, once the harness is ready, independently of later Held Messages.

QueueReason.description: One reason a Session has not started, for a Client to phrase.

branch.description: Omitted, a branch of the Workspace's own. A continuation runs on the branch of the Workspace it continues.

continues.description: The sealed Workspace this one carries on from, by its generated name, its identifier, any unambiguous prefix of its identifier, or `latest`.

model.description: The model the first Session runs on. Omitted, the Agent's, then the Harness's default.

mode.description: The mode the first Session runs in. Omitted, the Agent's, then the Harness's default.

thought_level.description: The thought level the first Session runs at. Omitted, the Agent's, then the Harness's default.

brief.description: The Brief the Workspace starts with, handed to the agent exactly as given. Omitted, the first Session waits for its first message to become the Brief.

participant.description: The name the Brief is written under. Omitted, its source is the operator and no one joins.

depends_on.description: Sessions of the Organization the new Session waits on, each named as a Session is anywhere else. It is dispatched only once every one has ended successfully. One the Organization does not have is refused with 404, and one that ended without success or is unreachable with 409; either refusal leaves nothing behind. No request adds a Dependency to a Session that already exists.

participant.description: The person posting, by declared name. Trimmed, 1 to 64 characters with no control characters, and never the name of an Agent in the Organization.
The person who wrote the message, by declared name. Trimmed, 1 to 64 characters with no control characters, and never the name of an Agent in the Organization.

id.description: The Workspace's own sequence. Stable and never reused: a taken or withdrawn message keeps it.

session.description: The Session the message started or woke, if it started or woke one.

held_message.description: The Held Message the post left, if a Turn could not take it at once.

opened_with.description: The Agent its first Session runs unless that Session names another.

instance.description: The Instance its Sessions execute on, while one is kept.

held.description: Why its Instance is held for work that exists nowhere else, if it is.

held_messages.description: The messages the unfinished Session cannot take yet, in arrival order.

started_by.description: The Event a firing opened it for, or the Brief's author an operator opened it with. Null when neither names anyone.

pull_requests.description: One per repository fixed on the Workspace, in the checkout's order.

unfinished_session.description: The one Session the Workspace has not let go of, while it has one.

session.description: The Workspace's latest Session, as the Session read answers it; null before it has one.

queue.description: Where that Session stands in the Organization's queue; null when it is in none of the queue's lists.

QueueStanding.description: A Workspace's Session as the queue sees it: queued with a position or reasons, waiting with reasons and held input, or unbriefed with held input.

position.description: Its global place among eligible requests for an Active-Work Slot; null when blocked, not requesting a slot, or dispatch configuration is unknown.

pending_since.description: When the oldest input held for its next turn arrived.

state.description: A trailing Session has answered its Turn while work its agent started still runs: it holds its Active-Work Slot and its Instance, refuses seal, and is waiting once that work settles and its agent falls quiet.

availability.description: Unavailable when no inbound GitHub Integration in the Organization watches the repository and none has delivered a pull request from it: kestrel cannot learn its pull requests, which says nothing about whether any exist.

known.description: The pull requests learned from the declared branch in this repository; null when unavailable.

PullRequest.description: A Workspace's current value for one pull request, learned from a verified GitHub Event.

repository.description: The head repository fixed on the Workspace.

updated_at.description: When GitHub last changed it, as the Event or a read back of the pull request said.

event.description: The Event the value was learned from.

OptionChange.description: One option a person changes on a Session: exactly one of `option` (the id the harness reported) or `category` (model, mode or thought_level), and the value to set.

participant.description: The person making the change, by the participant name rule.

option.description: The harness option's id. Exactly one of option or category.

category.description: One of model, mode or thought_level. Exactly one of option or category.

ChangingOption.description: An option change a person asked for while a Session is live, held until the harness answers it (ADR-0041).

agent.description: Omitted, the Agent of the Workspace's latest Session.

depends_on.description: Sessions of the Organization the new Session waits on, each named as a Session is anywhere else. It is dispatched only once every one has ended successfully. One the Organization does not have is refused with 404, and one that ended without success or is unreachable with 409; either refusal leaves nothing behind. No request adds a Dependency to a Session that already exists.

state.description: A trailing Session has answered its Turn while work its agent started still runs: it holds its Active-Work Slot and its Instance, refuses seal, and is waiting once that work settles and its agent falls quiet.

preparing.description: The step an unbriefed Session is preparing on: provisioning from claim until its supervisor connects, cloning until its checkout is reported, starting_harness until the harness is up, and harness_ready once it is. Null in every other state.

model.description: What the Session names for its Harness's model, or null for its Harness's default.

mode.description: What the Session names for its Harness's mode, or null for its Harness's default.

thought_level.description: What the Session names for its Harness's thought level, or null for its Harness's default.

worked_model.description: The Model-category option's current value, kept current by the supervisor (ADR-0041).

title.description: The harness's own name for the conversation, or null until it says one.

changing_options.description: Option changes a person asked for while the Session is live, held until the harness answers each (ADR-0041).

commands.description: The commands the harness offers for this Session.

interrupting.description: Who asked the working Turn to stop, while the request is in flight.

usage.description: What the Harness has spent on the Session: the live figure while its agent works, otherwise the latest its Turn answer or the end of its trailing work reported.

diagnostic.description: Why the Session failed, from the evidence its supervisor established. Null when it has not failed, or failed with no evidence; its presence never makes the read fail (ADR-0052).

tools.description: Tool calls open in the current observation; empty whenever observation is unavailable.

units.description: Adapter units open in the current observation, such as a Claude background task or subagent; they keep a trailing Session trailing. Empty whenever observation is unavailable.

last_activity_at.description: When the trailing Session's agent last showed activity; null in every other state.

depends_on.description: The Sessions this one was declared to wait on, whether or not they have ended.

SessionObservation.description: Whether the Session's open work is currently observed. current: its supervisor sent a snapshot over its open link and is still reaching it; tools and units list that snapshot, empty when nothing is open. unavailable: nothing current is known, whatever the Session's state or lease; tools and units are empty and never mean nothing is open. Neither availability changes the Session's state or scheduling.

observed_at.description: When the control plane took the snapshot.

last.description: The last snapshot this control plane took for the Session, kept until the Session ends; null when it holds none, as after a restart.

LastObservation.description: A historical snapshot of the Session's open work: what was open at observed_at, not proof that it still runs or that the supervisor is reachable.

SessionOption.description: A harness config option, whole: what it is, what it may be and what it is now.

category.description: `mode`, `model`, `model_config`, `thought_level`, or the harness's own string, which may begin with `_`.

values.description: The offered values of an ungrouped select; empty for a grouped one and for a boolean.

groups.description: The offered values of a grouped select; empty for an ungrouped one.

warns_cache.description: Whether changing this option makes the next Turn re-read the context without the prompt cache. True for a Model, ThoughtLevel or ModelConfig option, except a category kestrel's per-harness table keeps the cache for; at 0.3 that is Claude's ThoughtLevel (ADR-0041).

SessionOptionCurrent.description: The current value: a value id for a select, a boolean for a toggle.

SessionCommand.description: A command the harness offers for the Session, as a composer lists it.

Interrupting.description: A person's request that a Session's working Turn stop.

participant.description: The person asking. Trimmed, 1 to 64 characters with no control characters, and never the name of an Agent in the Organization.

ProviderCredential.description: A credential as everything but the Session that carries it sees it.

owner.description: The person it belongs to, which never changes.

SubscriptionProfileLogin.description: A login as everything but the Session that carries it sees it.

name.description: The variable, or the path beneath the agent's home.

set_at.description: When it was last held, whether by a person or by a Session handing back a refreshed login.

IntegrationRegistration.description: A registration, by the kind of external system it connects to.

GithubRegistration.description: A connection to GitHub, watching one repository.

repository.description: The repository it watches, as owner/name.

installation.description: The ID of the installation the App was installed as.

carries.description: The directions it carries. Absent means both.

interval.description: How often the poll reads the App's Delivery log, as a duration such as `1m` or `PT30S`.

webhook_secret.description: The App's webhook secret. Given one, a Delivery that reaches kestrel's webhook is recorded on arrival; the repository is polled either way.

WebhookRegistration.description: A generic endpoint any producer can POST CloudEvents to. It carries inbound only.

secret.description: The secret a sender presents as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`.

carries.description: The directions it carries. Absent means inbound.

IntegrationState.description: Disabled pauses every use of an Integration and keeps everything it resumes with.

IntegrationChange.description: What maintenance may change; an omitted field keeps its value.

carries.description: Every direction it carries afterwards; a generic webhook carries inbound only.

interval.description: How often a GitHub Integration's poll reads its App's Delivery log, as a positive duration.

revision.description: The revision this change was decided against.

IntegrationPrivateKeyReplacement.description: A replacement for the private key a GitHub Integration signs as its App with. The App, installation and repository it is checked against are the Integration's own and cannot be named.

private_key.description: The App's RSA private key, in PEM.

revision.description: The revision this replacement was decided against.

Integration.description: A registered Integration. What it presents to the external system is never part of it.

repository.description: The repository a GitHub Integration watches.

bot_login.description: The App's own bot account, `<slug>[bot]`, learned from GitHub when a GitHub Integration was registered.

revision.description: Bumped by every change, so a Client can say which one it decided against.

polled_every.description: How often it is polled, when it is.

webhook_path.description: Where on the link GitHub, or a generic producer, can deliver to it. An inbound GitHub Integration is also polled.

diagnostic.description: Why its use is paused now, with the steps that resume it; null while nothing is.

EventRefusal.description: The latest Event an Integration refused rather than stored, or the Deliveries it lost to GitHub's retention, visible until acknowledged.

id.description: The refused Event's id; null when Deliveries were lost rather than one refused.

EventRecord.description: An Event as kestrel recorded it.

record.description: kestrel's own identifier for the record.

integration.description: The Integration that recorded it. Null for an Event kestrel minted itself.

firings.description: What each Trigger that matched it did, oldest first.

Firing.description: One Trigger matching the Event, and what that match did.

workspace.description: The Workspace it opened or fed.

failure.description: Why a failed firing started nothing, such as labels choosing two Agents.

CloudEvent.description: The Event's CloudEvents envelope and payload.

Activity.description: Read-time summary of omitted narration and detail between consecutive shared-state entries. first_seq identifies the whole Activity, including selected kinds, and stays stable across pages and reconnects. last_seq is the highest Activity seq examined; its SSE id advances the global cursor. A closed replacement precedes the closing shared-state entry even when no detail was added. No summary is stored.

started_at.description: Earliest start among omitted unexpired entries.

finished_at.description: Latest finish among omitted unexpired entries.

anomaly.description: An omitted call was interrupted or unresolved.

closed.description: The next shared-state boundary has been examined. Followers replace open summaries by first_seq and CLI followers print only this final replacement.

Recorded.description: One Transcript entry, and where it sits in the order.

ExpiredEntry.description: Narration or detail expired in place after 30 days from append, including in sealed Workspaces. The enclosing record retains its original kind, seq and appended_at, with session_id null; all content, completion metadata and payload references are removed.

expired_at.description: When the sweep replaced the entry.

Entry.description: One completed unit of the Workspace Transcript.

Brief.description: The instruction a Workspace started with, rendered by the Trigger that fired or supplied by an operator.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

BriefSource.description: Who supplied a Brief: the Trigger whose firing rendered it, or an operator, under the participant name they declared if they declared one.

SessionStarted.description: A Session started on behalf of the Workspace.

Messages.description: Messages that arrived while a Session was active, drained as one Transcript entry.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

SpokenMessage.description: One Participant's message within a drained group.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

SessionEnded.description: A Session ended, and how it went.

TurnInterrupted.description: A person interrupted a working Turn without ending the Session.

because.description: Why it failed. Absent when it succeeded.

field.description: The request field the message concerns, when the refusal is about one.

DiagnosedRefusal.description: A typed Diagnostic, or the plain Refusal a refusal falls back to until its producer is typed. Only `kind` tells them apart.

Resource.description: A kind of record a reference, a declaration or an action names (ADR-0052).

Candidate.description: One record an ambiguous reference could have meant.

Consequence.description: What a destructive step does to work, typed so a Client never reads it from the consequence sentence.

ExplicitChoice.description: A destructive step is taken only by an explicit choice, whatever its consequence says; a Client never runs it as a default or automatic repair.

Diagnostic.description: Why kestrel would not do what it was asked, and the ordered, typed next steps that repair, inspect or retry it (ADR-0052). `message` is display only; a Client never classifies it.

organization.description: Null when the resource is not scoped to an Organization.

constraint.description: The existing author/name constraint the action violates, when established.

holding_session.description: The Session holding the conflicting state, when the conflict is one.

saved.description: What a write saved before the service it then asked could not answer.

provider_error.description: The provider's error type or code, never its message.

CredentialRejectedDiagnostic.description: A provider refused the credential itself when it was saved, so whatever was saved before is kept.

expired.description: Established only from evidence; never inferred from arbitrary harness output.

AuthenticationRequiredEvidence.description: The agent answered with ACP's authentication-required error.

methods.description: The ids of the ACP auth methods the agent offered.

method.description: The ACP auth method the supervisor was configured to log in with.

UnknownEvidence.description: What the agent said, bounded and redacted. It never establishes that a sign-in expired or is not covered.

Action.description: A typed corrective, inspective or retry step a Diagnostic offers, naming its own inputs rather than a shell command or browser route (ADR-0052). A Client binds it to a form, a flag or an API call.

missing.description: Which of this action's fixed inputs are not yet known, from `name`.
Which of this action's fixed inputs are not yet known, from `name`, `repositories`, `branch`.
Which of this action's fixed inputs are not yet known, from `name`, `harness`.
Which of this action's fixed inputs are not yet known, from `name`, `owner`.

name.description: The credential's variable. Its value is always collected privately and never serialized here.

consequence.description: Display-only explanation of the destructive effect; wording never decides whether confirmation is required.

ReplaceIntegrationPrivateKeyAction.description: Never carries the key: a Client reads it from a file or standard input when the step is taken.

consequence.description: Display-only explanation of the destructive effect; wording never decides whether confirmation is required.

sign_in.description: A safe locator for which sign-in to use, never held material.

compose.description: Whether Compose-specific checks apply, known only from the selected deployment's own evidence.

uncertain.description: Whether the operation's result is unknown, used after a lost write response. Never a signal to replay the write.

End.description: The control plane closed the stream on purpose. A stream that closes without one was cut off, and is resumed from the last id delivered.

because.description: `caught_up` when a read that does not follow has delivered every entry; `sealed` when the Workspace is sealed and every entry it will ever hold has been delivered.

TranscriptSessionState.description: Transient session_state SSE snapshot on every follow connect, then changes, including a change of observation availability. Never has an event id and never enters the Transcript. session_id is null when no unfinished Session exists, and observation is then unavailable; usage is the latest the Harness reported, live, or null.

usage.description: What the Harness has spent so far, held in memory beside the running tools while the Session is live and carried to followers; null until it reports one.

last_activity_at.description: When the agent last showed activity, present only while its Session trails its answer.

Event.description: SSE names: entry (Recorded), activity (Activity), session_state (TranscriptSessionState), cursor (CursorEvent), end (End), follower (FollowerEvent), or presence (Presence). Entry, Activity and cursor IDs advance the global Transcript cursor; session_state, follower and presence carry no id. Activity replacements retain first_seq, and their final closed replacement precedes the closing shared-state entry.

FollowerEvent.description: A follow that stayed open past caught-up registered: the id it renews by, and the lease in seconds it must renew before. Sent once per follow.

Presence.description: The whole current set of a Workspace's followers, sent when a follow registers and whenever the set changes. A named follow appears once per name, the follower's own included; unnamed follows are counted; an Agent never appears. Carries no Transcript cursor.

OptionChangedEntry.description: A person changed one of a Session's options between Turns (ADR-0041).

participant.description: The person who made the change.

option.description: The harness option's id, or the category when a queued Session's declared value changed.

from.description: What the option was set to before the change.

to.description: What it was set to; null when the harness refused.

refused.description: Why the harness refused, when it did.

PullRequestEntry.description: A verified GitHub Event observed a pull request from the Workspace's declared branch in one of its repositories. Learning it starts no work.

event.description: The Organization Event it was learned from.

repository.description: The head repository fixed on the Workspace.

InstanceReleased.description: A person released the Workspace's Instance, destroying it and whatever it held that was never pushed.

unpublished.description: What it held that existed nowhere else, as judged when it was released; null when it held nothing.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.
Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

CursorEvent.description: A cursor event carries the highest examined workspace:seq as its SSE id and data, so a filtered read resumes beyond omitted entries.

status.description: The status the Harness last reported for the call.

input.description: Inline JSON, or a PayloadReference when the serialized value exceeds 65536 bytes.

result.description: Inline JSON, or a PayloadReference when the serialized value exceeds 65536 bytes.

closing_reason.description: Why kestrel closed the call at a Turn boundary; null when the Harness settled it.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

RunningUnit.description: Work an adapter declared it runs apart from any tool call, such as a Claude background task, open until the adapter settles it. A settled unit adds no Transcript entry.

ChangesEvent.description: SSE names: open (ChangesOpen) on connect and on reconnect, change (Change) for one resource that changed, and resync (ChangesResync) for a subscriber that fell behind the bounded buffer. No event carries an id.

Change.description: One resource that changed: a Workspace or Session by id, with the name of the Workspace it belongs to, or the Organization's queue, which carries neither. Never a copy of its state.

Refetch.description: The event that means refetch every view the Client subscribes to. It carries no fields.

sessions.description: The blocking Sessions that have not ended successfully.

session.description: The Working or Trailing Session holding the Profile when it belongs to this Organization; otherwise null.

instance.description: The idle Instance being archived, or that dispatch will archive, to make room.

limit.description: The Organization's live Instance limit, reached with no idle Instance known recoverable.
The Active-Work Slot limit, every slot occupied.

sessions.description: Earlier eligible slot requests in this Organization, in global dispatch order.

elsewhere.description: Earlier eligible slot requests in other Organizations, omitted when zero.

participant.description: The participant who joined directly before the Brief, or null when the operator declared no name and no one joined.

workspace.description: The name of the Workspace that holds the Session.
The Workspace whose Transcript a `transcript` subscription follows, addressed as the Transcript read addresses it. Required for `transcript`.

after.description: The last Transcript cursor the tab saw. Absent means from the beginning.

kinds.description: Comma-separated Transcript kinds, as the Transcript read takes them.

participant.description: The name a `transcript` subscription's follower joins presence under, refused as the Transcript read's `as` is. Absent means anonymous.

StreamEvent.description: The event's name and `data` are those of the per-resource stream the subscription follows: an `Event` for a Transcript, a `ChangesEvent` for notices.

cursor.description: The subscription's Transcript cursor after this event, on entry, Activity and cursor events only. It resumes the subscription as `after`.

data.description: The per-resource stream's payload for this event name.
